@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+#
+# Check that cgroup-v2 cpuset.mems may name a private kmem node without
+# exposing it to ordinary allocations.
+#
+# Needs root, DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto> (see private_node_common.sh),
+# one common memory node and the cgroup-v2 cpuset controller.
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
+. "$DIR"/../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh
+. "$DIR"/private_node_common.sh
+
+TOOL="$DIR/kmem_private_rebind_tool"
+CG="$CGROOT/kmem-private-cpuset-$$"
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC2317 # invoked by the EXIT trap
+cleanup()
+{
+	pn_cpuset_cleanup "$CG"
+	pn_unbind_kmem_private
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+pn_setup
+[ -x "$TOOL" ] || pn_skip "kmem_private_rebind_tool not built"
+pn_find_common_nodes 1
+pn_require_mask_nodes "$PN" "${COMMON[0]}"
+pn_cpuset_cgroup "$CG"
+
+ktap_set_plan 4
+
+name="mixed common/private cpuset.mems is accepted"
+if echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "$PN"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="a private-only request keeps the node and inherits common memory"
+if echo "$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems")" "$PN" &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "$PN" &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "${COMMON[0]}"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="ordinary allocation in the cpuset stays on common memory"
+out=$(timeout 60 sh -c "echo \$\$ > '$CG/cgroup.procs'; exec '$TOOL' \
+	ordinary '$PN' '${COMMON[0]}' '${COMMON[0]}'")
+if [ "$out" = "private=0" ]; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_print_msg "$out"
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="removing the private node revokes it"
+if echo "${COMMON[0]}" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" 2>/dev/null &&
+   ! pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "$PN"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+ktap_finished
diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind.sh b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind.sh
new file mode 100755
index 000000000000..5d39be04f179
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,301 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+#
+# Check memory policies on private kmem memory while a cgroup-v2 cpuset is
+# reshaped, tasks move between cpusets, and the node is hotplugged. Each case
+# starts kmem_private_rebind_tool, changes the cpuset or the node, and sends
+# the tool SIGUSR1 to check where its memory went.
+#
+# Needs root, DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto> (see private_node_common.sh),
+# two common memory nodes and the cgroup-v2 cpuset controller.
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
+. "$DIR"/../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh
+. "$DIR"/private_node_common.sh
+
+TOOL="$DIR/kmem_private_rebind_tool"
+CG="$CGROOT/kmem-private-rebind-$$"
+CGCOMMON="$CGROOT/kmem-private-rebind-common-$$"
+OUT=$(mktemp)
+
+# CHILD is the timeout wrapper and TARGET the tool, which may be its child.
+stop_tool()
+{
+	[ -n "${TARGET:-}" ] && kill "$TARGET" 2>/dev/null
+	[ -n "${CHILD:-}" ] && kill "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null
+	[ -n "${CHILD:-}" ] && wait "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null
+	TARGET=
+	CHILD=
+}
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC2317 # invoked by the EXIT trap
+cleanup()
+{
+	stop_tool
+	rm -f "$OUT"
+	pn_cpuset_cleanup "$CG" "$CGCOMMON"
+	pn_unbind_kmem_private
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+wait_output()
+{
+	local pattern=$1 i
+
+	for ((i = 0; i < 100; i++)); do
+		grep -q "$pattern" "$OUT" && return 0
+		kill -0 "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null || break
+		sleep 0.1
+	done
+	return 1
+}
+
+# Start the tool in mode $1, inside cgroup $2 if given, and wait until it is
+# ready for the first SIGUSR1.
+start_tool()
+{
+	local mode=$1 cg=${2:-}
+
+	: > "$OUT"
+	if [ -n "$cg" ]; then
+		timeout 60 sh -ec "echo \$\$ > '$cg/cgroup.procs'; exec '$TOOL' \
+			'$mode' '$PN' '${COMMON[0]}' '${COMMON[1]}'" > "$OUT" 2>&1 &
+	else
+		timeout 60 "$TOOL" "$mode" "$PN" "${COMMON[0]}" "${COMMON[1]}" \
+			> "$OUT" 2>&1 &
+	fi
+	CHILD=$!
+	wait_output '^ready pid=' || return 1
+	TARGET=$(sed -n 's/^ready pid=//p' "$OUT")
+}
+
+# Signal the tool to check stage $1 and report its result as test $2.
+# Returns 1 if the tool did not answer.
+report_stage()
+{
+	local stage=$1 name=$2 line
+
+	if ! kill -USR1 "$TARGET" || ! wait_output "^stage=$stage "; then
+		ktap_print_msg "no answer from the tool"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	line=$(grep "^stage=$stage " "$OUT")
+	ktap_print_msg "$line"
+	if grep -q 'ok=1$' <<<"$line"; then
+		ktap_test_pass "$name"
+	else
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+	fi
+}
+
+# Run task policy mode $1 in the cpuset across one cpuset.mems change. The
+# tool's result is the last line of $OUT.
+run_task_policy()
+{
+	echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	if ! start_tool "$1" "$CG" ||
+	   ! echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" ||
+	   ! kill -USR1 "$TARGET" || ! wait "$CHILD"; then
+		stop_tool
+		echo "tool failed" >> "$OUT"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	CHILD=
+	TARGET=
+}
+
+# Allow or revoke the private node at stage $2, by attaching the tool to
+# another cpuset or by writing mask $3 to cpuset.mems, for action $1.
+transition_cpuset()
+{
+	local action=$1 stage=$2 mask=$3
+
+	case "$action:$stage" in
+	attach:1) echo "$TARGET" > "$CGCOMMON/cgroup.procs" ;;
+	attach:*) echo "$TARGET" > "$CG/cgroup.procs" ;;
+	*) echo "$mask" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" ;;
+	esac
+}
+
+# A private binding in tool mode $1 while its cpuset allows, revokes and
+# allows the private node again, by action reshape or attach.
+run_private_transitions()
+{
+	local mode=$1 label=$2 action=${3:-reshape}
+	local stage mask title cg=
+	local titles=("keeps private pages and placement while the node stays allowed"
+		"evacuates private pages and uses common placement when access is revoked"
+		"restores the original private request when access returns")
+
+	echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	if [ "$action" = attach ]; then
+		echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	fi
+	# Shared-policy parents and task-attachment tools start at the root.
+	if [ "$mode" = private-anon ] && [ "$action" = reshape ]; then
+		cg=$CG
+	fi
+	if ! start_tool "$mode" "$cg"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "tool setup failed"
+		for title in "${titles[@]}"; do
+			ktap_test_fail "$label $title"
+		done
+		stop_tool
+		return
+	fi
+	if [ "$mode" = private-shared ] && [ "$action" = reshape ]; then
+		echo "$TARGET" > "$CG/cgroup.procs"
+	fi
+	for stage in 0 1 2; do
+		mask=${COMMON[1]}
+		[ "$stage" = 1 ] || mask+=",$PN"
+		if ! transition_cpuset "$action" "$stage" "$mask"; then
+			ktap_print_msg "cannot change the cpuset"
+			ktap_test_fail "$label ${titles[$stage]}"
+			continue
+		fi
+		report_stage "$stage" "$label ${titles[$stage]}"
+	done
+	wait "$CHILD"
+	CHILD=
+	TARGET=
+}
+
+# Take the private node through stage $1: offline, common, offline, private.
+retype_node()
+{
+	case "$1" in
+	0|2) echo unplugged > "$D/state" ;;
+	1) echo 0 > "$D/private" && echo online_movable > "$D/state" ;;
+	3) echo 1 > "$D/private" && echo online_movable > "$D/state" ;;
+	esac
+}
+
+# A private binding in tool mode $1 while its node is hotplugged and retyped.
+run_private_retype()
+{
+	local mode=$1 label=$2
+	local stage name ready=false
+	local titles=("falls back while the private node is offline"
+		"binds the original node when it returns as common memory"
+		"falls back again after draining the common node"
+		"restores private placement when the node returns as private memory")
+
+	echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	start_tool "$mode" "$CG" && ready=true
+	for stage in 0 1 2 3; do
+		name="$label ${titles[$stage]}"
+		if [ "$ready" != true ]; then
+			ktap_print_msg "tool is not running"
+			ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		elif ! retype_node "$stage"; then
+			ktap_print_msg "cannot hotplug $(basename "$D")"
+			ktap_test_fail "$name"
+			ready=false
+		elif ! report_stage "$stage" "$name"; then
+			ready=false
+		fi
+	done
+	stop_tool
+	pn_bind_kmem_private "$D"
+}
+
+# A static binding in tool mode $1 of a common node that becomes private.
+run_common_retype()
+{
+	local mode=$1 name=$2 line
+
+	if ! echo unplugged > "$D/state" || ! echo 0 > "$D/private" ||
+	   ! echo online_movable > "$D/state"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "cannot provision common kmem memory"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		return
+	fi
+	echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	if ! start_tool "$mode" "$CG"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "tool setup failed"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		stop_tool
+		return
+	fi
+	if ! echo unplugged > "$D/state" || ! echo 1 > "$D/private" ||
+	   ! echo online_movable > "$D/state" ||
+	   ! echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "cannot retype kmem memory"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		stop_tool
+		return
+	fi
+	kill -USR1 "$TARGET"
+	if wait "$CHILD"; then
+		line=$(tail -1 "$OUT")
+		ktap_print_msg "$line"
+		if grep -q 'ok=1$' <<<"$line"; then
+			ktap_test_pass "$name"
+		else
+			ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		fi
+	else
+		ktap_print_msg "tool failed or timed out"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+	fi
+	CHILD=
+	TARGET=
+}
+
+pn_setup
+[ -x "$TOOL" ] || pn_skip "kmem_private_rebind_tool not built"
+pn_find_common_nodes 2
+pn_require_mask_nodes "$PN" "${COMMON[@]}"
+pn_cpuset_cgroup "$CG"
+pn_cpuset_cgroup "$CGCOMMON"
+echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" ||
+	ktap_exit_fail_msg "cannot set cpuset.mems of $CG"
+echo "${COMMON[1]}" > "$CGCOMMON/cpuset.mems" ||
+	ktap_exit_fail_msg "cannot set cpuset.mems of $CGCOMMON"
+
+ktap_set_plan 25
+
+run_task_policy interleave
+line=$(tail -1 "$OUT")
+ktap_print_msg "$line"
+name="interleave policy cannot reacquire private memory on rebind"
+if grep -q '^private=0 ' <<<"$line"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+run_task_policy bind
+line=$(tail -1 "$OUT")
+ktap_print_msg "$line"
+name="positional cpuset migration excludes private memory"
+if grep -q '^private=0 ' <<<"$line"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+name="removed common-node pages migrate to common fallback"
+if grep -q ' new_common=64$' <<<"$line"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+run_private_transitions private-anon "anonymous binding"
+run_private_transitions private-shared \
+	"shared binding across distinct mapper cpusets"
+run_private_transitions private-anon \
+	"anonymous binding across task attachment" attach
+run_private_transitions private-shared \
+	"shared binding across task attachment" attach
+run_private_retype retype-anon "anonymous private binding"
+run_private_retype retype-shared "shared private binding"
+run_common_retype static \
+	"shared common binding falls back after its node becomes private"
+run_common_retype static-mixed \
+	"shared common binding requires an allowed common target"
+
+ktap_finished
diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind_tool.c b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind_tool.c
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..3d88d1e61c2f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind_tool.c
@@ -0,0 +1,495 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+/*
+ * Helper for kmem_private_cpuset.sh and kmem_private_rebind.sh. Most modes
+ * place memory under a policy, print "ready pid=<pid>" and wait for SIGUSR1
+ * while the script changes the cpuset or the node, then report where the
+ * memory went. Modes with several stages wait for one SIGUSR1 per stage and
+ * print one "stage=<n> ... ok=<0|1>" line each.
+ *
+ * Modes that check their own results exit 1 when a check fails. All modes
+ * exit 2 on usage or setup errors.
+ */
+#define _GNU_SOURCE
+#include <linux/mempolicy.h>
+#include <signal.h>
+#include <stdbool.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#include <sys/mman.h>
+#include <sys/syscall.h>
+#include <sys/wait.h>
+#include <unistd.h>
+
+#ifndef MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES
+#define MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES (1 << 12)
+#endif
+
+#define NR_PAGES 64
+/* The kernel reads maxnode - 1 bits. */
+#define MAXNODE (8 * sizeof(unsigned long) + 1)
+
+enum mode {
+	ORDINARY,
+	INTERLEAVE,
+	BIND,
+	PRIVATE_ANON,
+	PRIVATE_SHARED,
+	RETYPE_ANON,
+	RETYPE_SHARED,
+	STATIC,
+	STATIC_MIXED,
+	NR_MODES,
+};
+
+static const struct {
+	const char *name;
+	const char *help;
+} modes[NR_MODES] = {
+	[ORDINARY] = { "ordinary", "allocate without a policy" },
+	[INTERLEAVE] = { "interleave",
+			 "task interleave over <private> and <common1>" },
+	[BIND] = { "bind", "task bind to <common1>" },
+	[PRIVATE_ANON] = { "private-anon",
+			   "private binding of anonymous memory" },
+	[PRIVATE_SHARED] = { "private-shared",
+			     "private binding of shared memory, two mappers" },
+	[RETYPE_ANON] = { "retype-anon",
+			  "private-anon across node hotplug" },
+	[RETYPE_SHARED] = { "retype-shared",
+			    "private-shared across node hotplug" },
+	[STATIC] = { "static", "static binding of shared memory to <private>" },
+	[STATIC_MIXED] = { "static-mixed",
+			   "static binding to <private> and <common1>" },
+};
+
+static void print_usage(const char *prog)
+{
+	int i;
+
+	fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <mode> <private> <common1> <common2>\n",
+		prog);
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_MODES; i++)
+		fprintf(stderr, "  %-15s %s\n", modes[i].name, modes[i].help);
+	exit(2);
+}
+
+/* Node masks are a single unsigned long. */
+static bool node_fits(int nid)
+{
+	return nid >= 0 && nid < (int)(8 * sizeof(unsigned long));
+}
+
+static void *map_anon(long len)
+{
+	return mmap(NULL, len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
+		    MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
+}
+
+static void *map_shared(int *fd, long len)
+{
+	*fd = memfd_create("private-rebind", 0);
+	if (*fd < 0 || ftruncate(*fd, len))
+		return MAP_FAILED;
+	return mmap(NULL, len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, *fd, 0);
+}
+
+static void announce_ready(void)
+{
+	printf("ready pid=%d\n", getpid());
+	fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+static long count_node(void *addr, long page_size, int nid)
+{
+	void *pages[NR_PAGES];
+	int status[NR_PAGES];
+	long i, count = 0;
+
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_PAGES; i++)
+		pages[i] = addr + i * page_size;
+	if (syscall(SYS_move_pages, 0, NR_PAGES, pages, NULL, status, 0UL))
+		return -1;
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_PAGES; i++)
+		count += status[i] == nid;
+	return count;
+}
+
+static bool range_matches(void *ptr, long page_size, unsigned char value)
+{
+	long i;
+
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_PAGES; i++)
+		if (*(unsigned char *)(ptr + i * page_size) != value)
+			return false;
+	return true;
+}
+
+static int bind_mapping(void *ptr, long len, unsigned long mask, int flags)
+{
+	return syscall(SYS_mbind, ptr, len, MPOL_BIND | flags,
+		       &mask, MAXNODE, 0UL);
+}
+
+static bool policy_matches(void *ptr, unsigned long mask, int flags)
+{
+	unsigned long actual = 0;
+	int mode;
+
+	return !syscall(SYS_get_mempolicy, &mode, &actual, MAXNODE,
+			ptr, MPOL_F_ADDR) &&
+		mode == (MPOL_BIND | flags) && actual == mask;
+}
+
+/* Report how many pages are on the private node. */
+static int ordinary(long page_size, int priv)
+{
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	void *ptr = map_anon(len);
+
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xab, len);
+	printf("private=%ld\n", count_node(ptr, page_size, priv));
+	return 0;
+}
+
+static void report_placement(void *ptr, long page_size, int priv,
+			     int common1, int common2)
+{
+	printf("private=%ld old_common=%ld new_common=%ld\n",
+	       count_node(ptr, page_size, priv),
+	       count_node(ptr, page_size, common1),
+	       count_node(ptr, page_size, common2));
+}
+
+/* Interleave over the private node and allocate after the cpuset change. */
+static int task_interleave(long page_size, int priv, int common1,
+			   int common2, const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = (1UL << common1) | (1UL << priv);
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	void *ptr;
+	int sig;
+
+	if (syscall(SYS_set_mempolicy, MPOL_INTERLEAVE, &mask, MAXNODE))
+		return 2;
+	announce_ready();
+	sigwait(waitset, &sig);
+	ptr = map_anon(len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xcd, len);
+	report_placement(ptr, page_size, priv, common1, common2);
+	munmap(ptr, len);
+	return 0;
+}
+
+/* Bind to the first common node and allocate before the cpuset change. */
+static int task_bind(long page_size, int priv, int common1, int common2,
+		     const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << common1;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	void *ptr;
+	int sig;
+
+	if (syscall(SYS_set_mempolicy, MPOL_BIND, &mask, MAXNODE))
+		return 2;
+	ptr = map_anon(len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xab, len);
+	announce_ready();
+	sigwait(waitset, &sig);
+	report_placement(ptr, page_size, priv, common1, common2);
+	munmap(ptr, len);
+	return 0;
+}
+
+struct shared_result {
+	long private_pages;
+	long shared_pages;
+};
+
+/* Keep one mapper outside the cpuset that is being changed. */
+static int shared_mapper(void *ptr, long len, long page_size, int priv,
+			 int common, int requests, int replies, pid_t child)
+{
+	struct shared_result result;
+	int stage, status;
+	bool contents;
+	void *range;
+
+	while (read(requests, &stage, sizeof(stage)) == sizeof(stage)) {
+		range = ptr + (stage + 4) * len;
+		memset(range, 0xef, len);
+		result.private_pages = count_node(range, page_size, priv);
+
+		/* Existing shared pages are not reallocated for another mapper. */
+		range = ptr + (stage + 1) * len;
+		contents = range_matches(range, page_size, 0xcd);
+		result.shared_pages = count_node(range, page_size,
+						 stage == 1 ? common : priv);
+		if (!contents)
+			result.shared_pages = -1;
+		if (write(replies, &result, sizeof(result)) != sizeof(result))
+			break;
+	}
+	close(requests);
+	close(replies);
+	if (waitpid(child, &status, 0) != child || !WIFEXITED(status))
+		return 1;
+	return WEXITSTATUS(status);
+}
+
+/*
+ * A private binding across three cpuset changes that allow, revoke and allow
+ * the node again. Range 0 of the mapping is populated up front and range
+ * 1 + stage at each stage. For shared memory the parent stays outside the
+ * cpuset as a second mapper and populates range 4 + stage.
+ */
+static int private_rebind(bool shared, long page_size, int priv, int common,
+			  const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << priv;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	long total = (shared ? 7 : 4) * len;
+	int fd = -1, requests[2], replies[2];
+	int stage, sig, failed = 0;
+	struct shared_result other;
+	long private_pages, common_pages, existing, existing_common;
+	bool policy, contents, ok;
+	pid_t child;
+	void *ptr, *range;
+
+	if (shared)
+		ptr = map_shared(&fd, total);
+	else
+		ptr = map_anon(total);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED ||
+	    bind_mapping(ptr, total, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES))
+		return 2;
+	/* Keep later ranges absent until their respective cpuset transition. */
+	if (madvise(ptr, total, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE))
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xab, len);
+	if (count_node(ptr, page_size, priv) != NR_PAGES)
+		return 1;
+
+	if (shared) {
+		if (pipe(requests) || pipe(replies))
+			return 2;
+		child = fork();
+		if (child < 0)
+			return 2;
+		if (child) {
+			close(requests[1]);
+			close(replies[0]);
+			failed = shared_mapper(ptr, len, page_size, priv, common,
+					       requests[0], replies[1], child);
+			goto out;
+		}
+		close(requests[0]);
+		close(replies[1]);
+		/* Populate the child's PTEs before cpuset-requested migration. */
+		if (!range_matches(ptr, page_size, 0xab))
+			return 2;
+	}
+
+	announce_ready();
+	for (stage = 0; stage < 3; stage++) {
+		if (sigwait(waitset, &sig))
+			return 2;
+		range = ptr + (stage + 1) * len;
+		memset(range, 0xcd, len);
+		private_pages = count_node(range, page_size, priv);
+		common_pages = count_node(range, page_size, common);
+		/* File-backed PTEs can be populated lazily after fork. */
+		contents = range_matches(ptr, page_size, 0xab);
+		existing = count_node(ptr, page_size, priv);
+		existing_common = count_node(ptr, page_size, common);
+		policy = policy_matches(ptr, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES);
+		ok = policy && contents;
+		/* Old pages leave the private node only once it is revoked. */
+		if (stage == 0)
+			ok &= existing == NR_PAGES && existing_common == 0;
+		else
+			ok &= existing == 0 && existing_common == NR_PAGES;
+		if (stage == 1)
+			ok &= common_pages == NR_PAGES && private_pages == 0;
+		else
+			ok &= private_pages == NR_PAGES && common_pages == 0;
+		other.private_pages = -1;
+		other.shared_pages = -1;
+		if (shared) {
+			if (write(requests[1], &stage, sizeof(stage)) != sizeof(stage) ||
+			    read(replies[0], &other, sizeof(other)) != sizeof(other))
+				return 2;
+			ok &= other.private_pages == NR_PAGES &&
+				other.shared_pages == NR_PAGES;
+		}
+		printf("stage=%d private=%ld common=%ld existing_private=%ld ",
+		       stage, private_pages, common_pages, existing);
+		printf("existing_common=%ld ", existing_common);
+		printf("policy=%d other_private=%ld shared_pages=%ld ok=%d\n",
+		       policy, other.private_pages, other.shared_pages, ok);
+		fflush(stdout);
+		failed |= !ok;
+	}
+	if (shared) {
+		close(requests[1]);
+		close(replies[0]);
+	}
+out:
+	munmap(ptr, total);
+	if (fd >= 0)
+		close(fd);
+	return failed;
+}
+
+/*
+ * A private binding while the node goes offline, returns as common memory,
+ * goes offline again and returns as private memory. Range @stage of the
+ * mapping is populated at each stage.
+ */
+static int private_retype(bool shared, long page_size, int target, int common,
+			  const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << target;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	long private_pages, common_pages;
+	int fd = -1, stage, sig, i, failed = 0;
+	bool policy, contents, ok;
+	void *ptr, *range;
+
+	if (shared)
+		ptr = map_shared(&fd, 4 * len);
+	else
+		ptr = map_anon(4 * len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED ||
+	    bind_mapping(ptr, 4 * len, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES) ||
+	    madvise(ptr, 4 * len, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE))
+		return 2;
+
+	/* Keep the policy alive without preventing the initial hot-unplug. */
+	announce_ready();
+	for (stage = 0; stage < 4; stage++) {
+		if (sigwait(waitset, &sig))
+			return 2;
+		range = ptr + stage * len;
+		memset(range, 0xa0 + stage, len);
+		private_pages = count_node(range, page_size, target);
+		common_pages = count_node(range, page_size, common);
+		policy = policy_matches(ptr, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES);
+		contents = true;
+		for (i = 0; i <= stage; i++)
+			contents &= range_matches(ptr + i * len, page_size,
+						  0xa0 + i);
+		ok = policy && contents;
+		if (stage & 1)
+			ok &= private_pages == NR_PAGES && common_pages == 0;
+		else
+			ok &= private_pages == 0 && common_pages == NR_PAGES;
+		printf("stage=%d target=%ld common=%ld policy=%d contents=%d ok=%d\n",
+		       stage, private_pages, common_pages, policy, contents, ok);
+		fflush(stdout);
+		failed |= !ok;
+	}
+	munmap(ptr, 4 * len);
+	if (fd >= 0)
+		close(fd);
+	return failed;
+}
+
+/*
+ * A static binding of shared memory to a common node, optionally with a
+ * second common node, that the script turns private before a second mapper
+ * faults the pages in.
+ */
+static int common_retype(bool mixed, long page_size, int target,
+			 int old_common, int new_common,
+			 const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << target;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	long private_pages, common_pages;
+	int fd, sig;
+	bool policy, ok;
+	void *ptr, *other;
+
+	if (mixed)
+		mask |= 1UL << old_common;
+	ptr = map_shared(&fd, len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED ||
+	    bind_mapping(ptr, len, mask, MPOL_F_STATIC_NODES))
+		return 2;
+	other = mmap(NULL, len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
+	if (other == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	/* No resident pages: the target can be removed and retyped. */
+	announce_ready();
+	if (sigwait(waitset, &sig))
+		return 2;
+	memset(other, 0xcd, len);
+	private_pages = count_node(other, page_size, target);
+	common_pages = count_node(other, page_size, new_common);
+	policy = policy_matches(other, mask, MPOL_F_STATIC_NODES);
+	ok = private_pages == 0 && common_pages == NR_PAGES && policy;
+	printf("private=%ld common=%ld policy=%d ok=%d\n",
+	       private_pages, common_pages, policy, ok);
+	munmap(other, len);
+	munmap(ptr, len);
+	close(fd);
+	return !ok;
+}
+
+int main(int argc, char **argv)
+{
+	long page_size = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
+	int priv, common1, common2, mode;
+	sigset_t waitset;
+
+	if (argc != 5)
+		print_usage(argv[0]);
+	for (mode = 0; mode < NR_MODES; mode++)
+		if (!strcmp(argv[1], modes[mode].name))
+			break;
+	if (mode == NR_MODES)
+		print_usage(argv[0]);
+	priv = atoi(argv[2]);
+	common1 = atoi(argv[3]);
+	common2 = atoi(argv[4]);
+	if (!node_fits(priv) || !node_fits(common1) || !node_fits(common2)) {
+		fprintf(stderr, "node ids must be 0 to %zu\n",
+			8 * sizeof(unsigned long) - 1);
+		return 2;
+	}
+
+	sigemptyset(&waitset);
+	sigaddset(&waitset, SIGUSR1);
+	sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, &waitset, NULL);
+
+	switch (mode) {
+	case ORDINARY:
+		return ordinary(page_size, priv);
+	case INTERLEAVE:
+		return task_interleave(page_size, priv, common1, common2,
+				       &waitset);
+	case BIND:
+		return task_bind(page_size, priv, common1, common2, &waitset);
+	case PRIVATE_ANON:
+	case PRIVATE_SHARED:
+		return private_rebind(mode == PRIVATE_SHARED, page_size, priv,
+				      common2, &waitset);
+	case RETYPE_ANON:
+	case RETYPE_SHARED:
+		return private_retype(mode == RETYPE_SHARED, page_size, priv,
+				      common2, &waitset);
+	case STATIC:
+	case STATIC_MIXED:
+		return common_retype(mode == STATIC_MIXED, page_size, priv,
+				     common1, common2, &waitset);
+	}
+	return 2;
+}
diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/dax/private_node_common.sh b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/private_node_common.sh
index cd03d9489822..5c58f3195d22 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/dax/private_node_common.sh
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/private_node_common.sh
@@ -234,3 +234,35 @@ pn_require_mask_nodes()
 			pn_skip "node $nid does not fit the helper node mask"
 	done
 }
+
+# Create cgroup $1 with the cpuset controller enabled and all CPUs.
+pn_cpuset_cgroup()
+{
+	[ "$(stat -fc %T "$CGROOT" 2>/dev/null)" = cgroup2fs ] ||
+		pn_skip "requires cgroup v2"
+	grep -qw cpuset "$CGROOT/cgroup.controllers" 2>/dev/null ||
+		pn_skip "cpuset controller unavailable"
+	if ! grep -qw cpuset "$CGROOT/cgroup.subtree_control"; then
+		echo +cpuset > "$CGROOT/cgroup.subtree_control" 2>/dev/null ||
+			pn_skip "cannot enable cpuset controller"
+		PN_CPUSET_ENABLED=1
+	fi
+	if ! mkdir "$1" ||
+	   ! cat "$CGROOT/cpuset.cpus.effective" > "$1/cpuset.cpus"; then
+		ktap_exit_fail_msg "cannot create $1"
+	fi
+}
+
+# Remove the cgroups $@ made by pn_cpuset_cgroup(), and the cpuset
+# controller if it enabled it.
+pn_cpuset_cleanup()
+{
+	local cg
+
+	for cg in "$@"; do
+		[ -d "$cg" ] && rmdir "$cg" 2>/dev/null
+	done
+	[ -n "${PN_CPUSET_ENABLED:-}" ] || return 0
+	PN_CPUSET_ENABLED=
+	echo -cpuset > "$CGROOT/cgroup.subtree_control" 2>/dev/null
+}

series_items.subject: [PATCH 60/60] Documentation/mm: describe private memory nodes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds documentation to describe private memory nodes, including how to create and manage them using DAX kmem private mode, binding memory to them, controlling access with cpusets, handling node unavailability or fullness, shared memory placement, and memory management services. It also updates the cgroup guides to reflect that cpuset memory migration never targets a private node and only moves pages off when the cpuset no longer allows it.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the documentation for 'cpuset.mems.effective' is inconsistent, listing it as a place where private nodes are removed from, but also mentioning that tasks do not allocate from it; requested clarification on how this affects memory migration and allocation.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Add Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst for administrators,
covering:
  - creating a private node with dax kmem private mode.
  - binding memory to it with MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES, and explicit
    migration.
  - controlling access with cpusets.
  - what happens when the node becomes unavailable or full.
  - shared memory placement.
  - which memory management services apply, and how memory counters
    account private memory.

In both cgroup guides, document that cpuset memory migration never
targets a private node and moves pages off one only when the cpuset no
longer allows it. Document how a private-only cpuset.mems gains the
parent's common memory nodes in v2, and is rejected in v1.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

 Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.rst         |  13 +-

 4 files changed, 243 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

 Also if 'cpuset.memory_migrate' is set true, then if that cpuset's

diff --git a/Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst b/Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..2fedf7534446
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+.. SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+
+====================
+Private memory nodes
+====================
+
+A private memory node is a NUMA node whose memory the kernel does not use for
+ordinary allocations. Applications place memory there only by asking for that
+node explicitly. This keeps specialized memory, such as HBM or coherent device
+memory, visible as a NUMA node without making it a general fallback for every
+allocation. Memory that is not private is called common memory.
+
+The kernel manages a private node's memory with the usual page allocator. The
+driver that provides the memory decides which memory management services the
+node also gets. The dax kmem private mode described below enables reclaim,
+compaction and explicit placement by applications.
+
+``/sys/devices/system/node/has_private_memory`` lists the private nodes, and
+``has_common_memory`` lists the others. Together they make up ``has_memory``.
+
+Creating a private node
+=======================
+
+Private memory is added through memory hotplug and requires ``CONFIG_NUMA``.
+With ``CONFIG_DEV_DAX_KMEM`` and ``CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE``, a device-dax
+instance bound to ``kmem`` can be onlined as private memory. Select private mode
+while the device's memory is unplugged::
+
+    echo unplugged > /sys/bus/dax/devices/daxX.Y/state
+    echo 1 > /sys/bus/dax/devices/daxX.Y/private
+    echo online_movable > /sys/bus/dax/devices/daxX.Y/state
+
+The ``private`` attribute defaults to 0, which keeps ordinary kmem behavior.
+Its value can change only while the device is unplugged. Unbinding kmem
+discards the setting. Bind the device with memory auto-onlining disabled, so
+that its memory is not onlined as common memory first.
+
+All System RAM on a node shares one configuration. Adding memory with a
+different configuration to a node that already has System RAM fails with
+``-EBUSY``. To change the configuration, remove every System RAM block on the
+node first. Offlining the blocks is not enough, since offline blocks keep their
+configuration so they can be onlined again.
+
+A private node may have CPUs. Like the CPUs of a memoryless node, they get
+ordinary memory from the nearest common nodes.
+
+Using private memory
+====================
+
+An application binds an anonymous or shmem-backed mapping to one private node
+with ``mbind(2)``, passing ``MPOL_BIND | MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES``, before it
+faults the pages in::
+
+    buf = mmap(NULL, length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
+               MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
+    /* mask contains exactly the chosen private node */
+    mbind(buf, length, MPOL_BIND | MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES, mask, maxnode, 0);
+    memset(buf, 0, length);
+
+``mbind(2)`` rejects a private binding with ``-EINVAL`` if:
+
+- the mask names more than one node, or a node that is not private memory
+  with userspace placement enabled.
+- the mode is not ``MPOL_BIND``, or the flag is combined with
+  ``MPOL_F_STATIC_NODES``, ``MPOL_F_RELATIVE_NODES`` or
+  ``MPOL_F_NUMA_BALANCING``.
+- the mapping is a HugeTLB mapping. Private nodes hold no HugeTLB pages.
+- the node is not in the caller's cpuset.
+
+Kernels without private node support reject the flag with ``-EINVAL``, so
+applications can probe for it. ``get_mempolicy(2)`` reports the flag.
+
+Without ``MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES``, private nodes in a ``set_mempolicy(2)`` or
+``mbind(2)`` mask are ignored, as nodes outside the cpuset are. A mask that
+names only private nodes is therefore rejected with ``-EINVAL``.
+``set_mempolicy(2)`` does not accept the flag, because a task policy also
+applies to the kernel's allocations on behalf of the task. Preferred,
+interleave and preferred-many policies, tmpfs ``mpol=`` mount options, HugeTLB
+pools and automatic NUMA balancing use only common memory.
+
+``move_pages(2)`` and ``migrate_pages(2)`` can move pages to a private node
+with userspace placement enabled, subject to their usual permission checks.
+They take no flag. ``move_pages(2)`` rejects other private nodes with
+``-ENODEV``, and ``migrate_pages(2)`` ignores them, as it ignores nodes outside
+the caller's cpuset.
+
+Page cache for regular files is never allocated from private memory.
+Copy-on-write pages of a private file mapping follow a binding like anonymous
+memory, and explicit migration can move existing file pages to a private node.
+A private binding on a shmem-backed mapping allocates its pages from the
+private node, and reclaim swaps them out like other shmem pages.
+
+guest_memfd memory cannot be moved, so a binding places it on a private node
+only if the node has memory onlined as ``online`` or ``online_kernel``.
+
+Controlling access
+==================
+
+``cpuset.mems`` includes private nodes by default, so any task can bind to a
+private node and use up its capacity. Use ``cpuset.mems`` to limit which tasks
+may use a private node. Listing a private node in ``cpuset.mems`` permits
+private bindings to it. Tasks do not otherwise allocate from it.
+
+In cgroup v2, a ``cpuset.mems`` that names only private nodes is accepted, and
+the parent's common nodes are added to ``cpuset.mems.effective`` so that tasks
+always have memory for ordinary allocations. The parent's other private nodes
+are not added. An empty ``cpuset.mems`` inherits the parent's effective nodes,
+private nodes included.
+
+In cgroup v1, writing a ``cpuset.mems`` that names only private nodes, or
+attaching a task to such a cpuset, fails with ``-ENOSPC``. When memory hotplug
+leaves a v1 cpuset with only private memory, its tasks move to an ancestor.
+
+Cpuset memory migration never moves pages to a private node. It moves pages
+off a private node only when the cpuset no longer allows that node.
+
+When a node becomes unavailable
+===============================
+
+A private binding applies while its node is online private memory with
+userspace placement enabled and the task's cpuset allows it. While it applies,
+allocations use only that node and never fall back to common memory.
+
+Otherwise the binding is suspended and allocations use the task's common
+memory. The binding is never rebound to another node. It applies again when
+its node becomes available again. If the node comes back as common memory, the
+binding acts like an ordinary binding to that node. ``get_mempolicy(2)`` keeps
+reporting the original binding throughout.
+
+==============================  ==================  =========================
+Event                           New allocations     Existing private pages
+==============================  ==================  =========================
+cpuset removes the node         common memory       migrated to common memory
+cpuset allows the node again    the private node    not migrated back
+node is being hot-removed       the private node    migrated to common memory
+node is removed                 common memory       none remain
+node returns as private memory  the private node
+node returns as common memory   that common node
+==============================  ==================  =========================
+
+While a node is being hot-removed, its free memory is no longer available, so
+faults on mappings bound to it can fail with ``SIGBUS`` until removal finishes.
+
+Allocations that cannot use ``ZONE_MOVABLE``, such as guest_memfd memory, ignore
+a binding to a private node whose memory is all movable and use common memory.
+Long-term pins migrate pages out of ``ZONE_MOVABLE`` as usual.
+
+An ordinary policy that is not rebound, such as a static binding or a shared
+memory policy, can name a node that later comes back as private memory. If the
+task may use no common node in such a policy, the policy is ignored and the
+allocation uses common memory.
+
+Exhaustion and OOM
+==================
+
+A private node is a fixed pool, like a HugeTLB pool. When the node is full and
+reclaim cannot free enough memory on it, an allocation for a private binding
+fails without invoking the OOM killer and without falling back to common
+memory. A page fault then gets ``SIGBUS``, as with an exhausted HugeTLB pool.
+Other callers see an error, such as ``-ENOMEM`` from ``write(2)`` to a shmem
+file or ``-EFAULT`` from a write through ``/proc/pid/mem`` or
+``process_vm_writev(2)``. Allocations succeed again once memory on the node is
+freed.
+
+Private pages are charged to memory cgroups like other memory. Reaching a
+memory cgroup limit causes reclaim and OOM handling as usual, and memcg reclaim
+also reclaims private nodes that permit reclaim.
+
+Tasks whose cpusets overlap only on private nodes are not chosen as OOM victims
+for each other.
+
+Shared memory
+=============
+
+A private binding on a shmem-backed mapping, such as memfd, tmpfs or shared
+anonymous memory, applies to the file's offset range, not to each task that
+maps it. Whether a new page is allocated on the private node depends on the
+cpuset of the task that faults it in. A task whose cpuset excludes the node
+allocates the page on common memory, and every task that maps the file then
+uses that page. A file can therefore hold both private and common pages.
+
+Shared pages keep using private memory until they are freed. Unmapping the
+file does not free them while the file still exists or another task keeps it
+open. Truncate the file or punch holes in it to return the memory.
+
+Memory management services
+==========================
+
+kswapd and kcompactd run on a private node only if its driver enables reclaim
+and compaction, as the dax kmem private mode does. Writing to ``nodeN/reclaim``
+or ``nodeN/compact`` fails with ``-EOPNOTSUPP`` for a private node without the
+service. ``MADV_COLD``, ``MADV_PAGEOUT`` and ``MADV_FREE`` act only on pages on
+nodes that permit reclaim.
+
+Private nodes are excluded from KSM merging, THP collapse, automatic NUMA
+balancing, DAMON actions, demotion between memory tiers and HugeTLB pool
+growth. A KSM page that is explicitly migrated to a private node remains
+shareable while it is mapped.
+
+Memory hot-remove and soft offline migrate pages on a private node to common
+memory. Pinned or otherwise unmovable pages can still prevent removal.
+
+Accounting
+==========
+
+``MemTotal`` and ``MemFree`` in ``/proc/meminfo`` include private memory with
+userspace placement enabled, such as dax kmem private memory, since it holds
+ordinary application data. They leave out other private memory. The overcommit
+limit (``CommitLimit``) and other limits sized from total memory follow
+``MemTotal``.
+
+``MemAvailable`` and the dirty page limits count free memory on common nodes
+only, since free private memory serves only private bindings. ``MemTotal``
+minus ``MemAvailable`` therefore includes free private memory.
+
+Per-node statistics, including ``nodeN/meminfo``, ``/proc/vmstat`` and
+``memory.numa_stat``, count all memory, private memory included.
+
+Limitations
+===========
+
+- A task's OOM score includes its resident private pages.
+- Free page reporting reports free private pages like other free pages.

--

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new set of functions to iterate over nodes based on their state, such as online or memory state. It adds iterators for walking through node states and provides helpers for intersecting nodemasks with specific node states. This allows developers to easily traverse the system's nodes based on their current state, making it easier to manage and optimize system resources.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the behavior of N_MEMORY_COMMON and its relationship to N_MEMORY, specifically how it affects allocation targets and MM services. The author explains that N_MEMORY_COMMON takes the second meaning of N_MEMORY (ordinary allocations and MM services can use this node's memory) and converts the users of N_MEMORY accordingly. They also clarify that unless a system has a private node, N_MEMORY and N_MEMORY_COMMON are the same set, so behavior should be unchanged.
review_comments.raw_body:
This is v6 of the Private NUMA node series. The series falls into four
parts, each building on the one before:

   1-18  mm: introduce N_MEMORY_COMMON
  19-26  restrict folio-walking MM services to common memory
  27-44  N_MEMORY_PRIVATE, kept out of cpusets, mempolicy, accounting
         and the page allocator's ordinary paths
  45-61  private node features, memory hotplug of private memory,
         dax/kmem private mode, selftests and documentation

Patches 1-26 change no behavior on any system and can be reviewed and
merged on their own. Without private nodes, every path in patches 27-61
behaves as before.

The full stack is also available at:
https://github.com/gourryinverse/linux/tree/scratch/gourry/managed_nodes/private_nodes_v6

Motivation
==========

Some memory should be visible as a NUMA node without becoming part of
the general allocation pool: HBM, coherent GPU or accelerator memory,
or device memory a driver hands out itself.

Today such memory is either ordinary System RAM, where any allocation
can fall back onto it and every MM service manages it, or ZONE_DEVICE,
where the buddy allocator and the MM services are not available at all.

Private nodes sit in between. Their memory is managed by the buddy
allocator, but ordinary allocations never land on it, and generic MM
services leave it alone unless the node opts back in.

Model
=====

  N_MEMORY = N_MEMORY_COMMON + N_MEMORY_PRIVATE

  - N_MEMORY keeps meaning "this node has memory".
  - N_MEMORY_COMMON means ordinary allocations and kernel services
    may use it.
  - Allocation isolation comes from the zonelists: a private node is
    on no fallback zonelist and has an empty __GFP_THISNODE zonelist.
    It is reached only through its own private zonelist.
  - Services that walk existing folios check folio_is_common_memory()
    where they already skip ZONE_DEVICE.
  - A private node can opt into compaction, reclaim and userspace
    placement through per-node features. The services are written in
    terms of their own node state (N_MEMORY_RECLAIM, ...), so services
    don't need to be "aware" of anything but themselves.

The node state use / filtering model goes as such:
  1) If you're walking the normal zonelists, you're already filtered
  2) If you're walking nodelists to touch memory, filter on
     N_MEMORY_COMMON by default (replacing N_MEMORY).
  3) If you're walking structures to operate on folios / pages,
     check folio_is_common_memory() (replacing zone_device checks)
  4) If the service allows private memory interactions, use the
     N_MEMORY_<FEATURE> bit corresponding to the service.

     e.g.: reclaim checks N_MEMORY_FEATURE when walking N_MEMORY
     or when walking the private memory zonelist.

N_MEMORY_COMMON (patches 1-18)
==============================

N_MEMORY has two meanings today:
  1) this node has memory
  2) ordinary allocations and MM services can use this node's memory

The two are the same today. They stop being the same once a NUMA node
with memory isn't part of the general allocation pool.

N_MEMORY_COMMON takes the second meaning, and the N_MEMORY users that
mean it are converted. N_MEMORY continues reporting memory topology.

The rule for choosing between them:

  N_MEMORY         the node has memory: topology, per-node metadata and
                   statistics, cpuset.mems.
  N_MEMORY_COMMON  ordinary allocations or a kernel service may use the
                   node's memory: zonelists, allocation and migration
                   targets, per-node service threads, and sizing or
                   accounting meant for ordinary allocations.

Code that walks the existing zonelist needs no check. The zonelists
are built from N_MEMORY_COMMON, so they already hold only memory the
allocation may use.

Unless a system actually has a private node, N_MEMORY and
N_MEMORY_COMMON are the same set, so behavior should be unchanged.

  1-3   node-state helpers, N_MEMORY_COMMON itself, and the
        `has_common_memory` sysfs ABI.
  4     zonelists: the fallback lists hold common nodes, and a node's
        __GFP_THISNODE list is built only for a common node
  5-11  allocation and migration targets
  12-13 kswapd and kcompactd
  14-18 sizing and accounting meant for ordinary allocations

has_common_memory lists the same nodes as has_memory until memory
outside N_MEMORY_COMMON exists. It is added now so that userspace, such
as libnuma, can start choosing allocation targets from it, and so that
the meaning is fixed before anything makes the two lists differ.

Folio-walking MM services (patches 19-26)
=========================================

Patches 1-18 decide where memory comes from: zonelists, allocation
targets and per-node services follow N_MEMORY_COMMON. Some MM services
instead reach folios that already exist, wherever they are: through
page tables (KSM, khugepaged, NUMA hinting, madvise, mbind() and
migrate_pages(), move_pages()) or through physical addresses (DAMON).

These services skip ZONE_DEVICE folios with folio_is_zone_device() and
page_is_zone_device().

Patch 19 generalizes those checks into folio_is_common_memory() and
page_is_common_memory(), which reject ZONE_DEVICE folios and folios
on a node outside N_MEMORY_COMMON.

The rule: a service that walks folios checks folio_is_common_memory()
where it would otherwise check folio_is_zone_device().

Rather than add new hooks to page-table and pfn walkers, this reuses the
places that already opt ZONE_DEVICE memory out.

  19    folio_is_common_memory() and page_is_common_memory()
  20-26 ZONE_DEVICE checks in folio-walking services become
        page/folio_is_common_memory(). One component per patch.

N_MEMORY_PRIVATE (patches 27-44)
================================

Patches 27-44 add the memory that makes N_MEMORY and N_MEMORY_COMMON
differ. A private node has online System RAM that ordinary allocations
do not use and MM services leave alone, so neither an allocation that
names no node nor a node-local kernel allocation can land on it.

Most of these patches add the explicit opt-outs that the N_MEMORY ->
N_MEMORY_COMMON conversion did not cover, largely concentrated in
cpuset, mempolicy and migration.

In the page allocator, each node gets a private zonelist holding its
own zones only if it is private. MM code reaches private memory only
through that zonelist (ALLOC_ZONELIST_PRIVATE plus a nodemask).

A private request whose node becomes ineligible relaxes onto common
memory, and exhausting private memory fails the allocation (SIGBUS on
fault) instead of invoking the OOM killer (this can change in the
future with additional work).

Nothing in patches 27-44 creates private memory. Memory hotplug of
private memory, with dax/kmem as its first user, comes in patches
56-57, after the feature bits that let a private node opt into
reclaim, compaction and userspace placement.

  27-28 N_MEMORY_PRIVATE, exported as has_private_memory.
        A per-node feature mask on the pgdat.
  29-30 accounting: MemTotal/MemFree/other limits ignore private mem.
        the auto-movable online policy ignores private memory
  31-35 cpusets and mempolicy: private nodes are inherited only on
        request, never rebound onto, never spread over, and never
        migrate_pages() destinations
  36    explicit reclaim and compaction requests refuse private nodes
  37-44 page allocator:
        37-38 the reserves and watermarks, and contiguous allocation,
              skip/refuse private memory
        39-40 the private zonelist and its selection by MM callers
        41    a private request whose node becomes ineligible relaxes
              onto common memory to ensure forward progress
        42    exhausting private memory fails with SIGBUS, like an
              exhausted HugeTLB pool
        43    an alloc_flags-aware folio allocator (Brendan Jackman)
        44    a bind policy whose nodes became private falls back to
              common memory

Private node features and providers (patches 45-61)
===================================================

Patches 1-44 keep every generic MM service off private memory.

Some private memory wants a few of them back: HBM or coherent GPU
memory that userspace manages with mbind() and migrate_pages() needs
reclaim and compaction, while staying out of incidental allocation
(no fallback onto it, only explicit placement).

Patches 45-55 add three opt-in feature bits and corresponding node
states:

  N_MEMORY_COMPACTION   kcompactd, proactive and explicit compaction
  N_MEMORY_RECLAIM      kswapd, memcg and explicit reclaim
  N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY    mbind() and explicit migration may target it

The states cover what the kernel does on its own initiative. Direct
reclaim and compaction serve an allocation within its own zonelist, so
an allocation from a private node may reclaim and compact it either way.

RECLAIM requires COMPACTION, and MEMPOLICY requires both. Userspace
control (mbind, migration) generates fragmentation, and as a result
private allocations would fail unpredictably without reclaim/compaction.

Relcaim and compaction are required by mempolicy because otherwise
order-N allocations cause unpredictable out of memory conditions due
to fragmentation.

Demotion and NUMA balancing support are deferred to a later series
but can be trivially support to allow demotions from HBM to DRAM
as a way of cheap tiering.

Every common node carries all three, so the existing N_MEMORY_COMMON
users that mean "reclaim" or "compaction" move to the new states.

Service support:

  45-46 N_MEMORY_COMPACTION, and compaction switched to it
  47-48 N_MEMORY_RECLAIM, and reclaim switched to it
  49    madvise reclaim advice only for reclaim-capable memory
  50    memcg reclaim also visits private nodes that permit reclaim
  51    N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY
  52    explicit migration acts on N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY memory
  53    N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY memory counts as general-purpose.
        MemAvailable (free and file pages) and dirty limits count
	only common memory.
  54    MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES: mbind() flag that binds a mapping to
        one private node.
  55    migrate_pages() support for N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY nodes

Creating a private node

  56    memory hotplug of private memory, with a feature mask
  57    dax/kmem private mode

Testing and Documentation:

  58-60 selftests: private kmem devices and services, memory policy
        bindings, migration and exhaustion, and cpuset interaction
  61    Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst

MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES is new uapi. Without it, private nodes in an
mbind() mask are ignored, similar to nodes outside the cpuset.

libnuma and numactl need a matching change to reach private nodes.

There is no sysfs list of the nodes that accept private bindings.
userspace can probe with MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES.  Otherwise - we can
discuss how service support should be discoverable to userspace.

Memory hotplug is the only source of private memory right now.

All System RAM on a node shares one configuration: hotplug with a
different one fails with -EBUSY.

Costs and known limits
======================

  - ZONELIST_PRIVATE is a third zonelist per pgdat; with NODES_SHIFT=10
    that is about 80KB per possible node, though a private zonelist
    holds at most one node's zones.

    local-only zonelists can be space-optimized if this matters.

  - Free page reporting reports free private pages like any others.

  - Tasks are OOM-scored by all of their resident memory,
    private pages included.

Changes since v5 ("Private Memory NUMA Nodes")
==============================================

  - Reordered so the N_MEMORY audit (patches 1-26) comes first and can
    be reviewed (and merged) on its own if desired.
  - Capabilities became memory features with node states, so a service
    can be written in terms of itself: reclaim walks N_MEMORY_RECLAIM,
    compaction N_MEMORY_COMPACTION.
  - The capability set is pared down to COMPACTION, RECLAIM and
    MEMPOLICY for the first run.  DEMOTION, NUMA_BALANCING, and
    compressed RAM support are deferred.
  - The private zonelist is now local-only. A fallback variant can be
    added if a use case needs one.
  - cpuset and OOM semantics are worked out:
      - cpuset.mems governs private nodes
      - private-only request inherits the parent's common nodes.
  - Private bindings are an explicit uapi flag, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES,
    rather than inferred from the nodemask.
  - Exhausting private placement fails the fault with SIGBUS, as an
    exhausted HugeTLB pool does, instead of invoking the OOM killer.
    OOM support can be added later, but this keeps initial support
    reasonable simple.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about restricting the node set for memory policy calculations and their per-node sysfs entries to N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes, explaining that this is because ordinary allocations should reach only common (general purpose) memory. The author confirmed that they will use N_MEMORY_COMMON for boot mempolicy calculations and their per-node sysfs entries, and restricted the node set mpol_set_nodemask() applies to set_mempolicy() and mbind() masks to N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Zonelists decide which nodes an allocation can reach.

The fallback lists hold every node in N_MEMORY, and a node's
__GFP_THISNODE list holds its own zones whatever the node's state.

Ordinary allocations should reach only common (general purpose) memory.

Build the fallback zonelists from N_MEMORY_COMMON, and __GFP_THISNODE
zonelists only for a common node.

The build_local_zonelist() refactor lets us reuse the code to build
a local-only zonelist for nodes outside the N_MEMORY_COMMON set later.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 23 ++++++++++++-----------
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+), 11 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index ddb04b72a160..0448d04e048a 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -5947,17 +5947,14 @@ int find_next_best_node_in(int node, nodemask_t *used_node_mask,
 }
 
 
-/*
- * Build __GFP_THISNODE zonelists
- */
-static void build_thisnode_zonelists(pg_data_t *pgdat)
+/* Build a local-only zonelist when this node is eligible. */
+static void build_local_zonelist(pg_data_t *pgdat, int zlidx, bool eligible)
 {
-	struct zoneref *zonerefs;
-	int nr_zones;
+	struct zoneref *zonerefs =
+		pgdat->node_zonelists[zlidx]._zonerefs;
 
-	zonerefs = pgdat->node_zonelists[ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK]._zonerefs;
-	nr_zones = build_zonerefs_node(pgdat, zonerefs);
-	zonerefs += nr_zones;
+	if (eligible)
+		zonerefs += build_zonerefs_node(pgdat, zonerefs);
 	zonerefs->zone = NULL;
 	zonerefs->zone_idx = 0;
 }
@@ -6001,8 +5998,12 @@ static void build_node_zonelist(pg_data_t *pgdat, const nodemask_t *candidates,
 
 static void build_zonelists(pg_data_t *pgdat)
 {
-	build_node_zonelist(pgdat, &node_states[N_MEMORY], ZONELIST_FALLBACK);
-	build_thisnode_zonelists(pgdat);
+	int nid = pgdat->node_id;
+
+	build_node_zonelist(pgdat, &node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON],
+			    ZONELIST_FALLBACK);
+	build_local_zonelist(pgdat, ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK,
+			     node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON));
 }
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_HAVE_MEMORYLESS_NODES

--

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Use N_MEMORY_COMMON for boot mempolicy calculations and their per-node
sysfs entries (weighted interleave weights).

Restrict the node set mpol_set_nodemask() applies to set_mempolicy()
and mbind() masks to N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes.

A tmpfs mpol= nodelist must name only N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes, and an
interleave policy without a nodelist defaults to them.

Later when an N_MEMORY node is omitted from the N_MEMORY_COMMON set,
they will be stripped from mempolicy nodemasks as they're not eligible
(similar to memoryless nodes today).

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/mempolicy.c | 30 +++++++++++++++---------------
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+), 15 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/mempolicy.c b/mm/mempolicy.c
index 6f800fb961ae..806577e1d48b 100644
--- a/mm/mempolicy.c
+++ b/mm/mempolicy.c
@@ -213,10 +213,10 @@ static void reduce_interleave_weights(unsigned int *bw, u8 *new_iw)
 	int nid;
 
 	/*
-	 * N_MEMORY can change while wi_state_lock is held. Remember the
-	 * nodes contributing to sum_bw so all passes use the same set.
+	 * N_MEMORY_COMMON can change while wi_state_lock is held. Remember
+	 * the nodes contributing to sum_bw so all passes use the same set.
 	 */
-	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY) {
+	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {
 		node_set(nid, nodes);
 		sum_bw += bw[nid];
 	}
@@ -439,9 +439,9 @@ static int mpol_set_nodemask(struct mempolicy *pol,
 	if (!pol || pol->mode == MPOL_LOCAL)
 		return 0;
 
-	/* Check N_MEMORY */
+	/* Check N_MEMORY_COMMON */
 	nodes_and(nsc->mask1,
-		  cpuset_current_mems_allowed, node_states[N_MEMORY]);
+		  cpuset_current_mems_allowed, node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]);
 
 	VM_BUG_ON(!nodes);
 
@@ -2104,7 +2104,7 @@ bool apply_policy_zone(struct mempolicy *policy, enum zone_type zone)
 	 * if policy->nodes has movable memory only,
 	 * we apply policy when gfp_zone(gfp) = ZONE_MOVABLE only.
 	 *
-	 * policy->nodes is intersect with node_states[N_MEMORY].
+	 * policy->nodes is intersect with node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON].
 	 * so if the following test fails, it implies
 	 * policy->nodes has movable memory only.
 	 */
@@ -3398,11 +3398,11 @@ void __init numa_policy_init(void)
 
 	/*
 	 * Set interleaving policy for system init. Interleaving is only
-	 * enabled across suitably sized nodes (default is >= 16MB), or
-	 * fall back to the largest node if they're all smaller.
+	 * enabled across suitably sized common memory nodes (default is
+	 * >= 16MB), or fall back to the largest node if they're all smaller.
 	 */
 	nodes_clear(interleave_nodes);
-	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY) {
+	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {
 		unsigned long total_pages = node_present_pages(nid);
 
 		/* Preserve the largest node */
@@ -3474,7 +3474,7 @@ int mpol_parse_str(char *str, struct mempolicy **mpol)
 		*nodelist++ = '\0';
 		if (nodelist_parse(nodelist, nodes))
 			goto out;
-		if (!nodes_subset(nodes, node_states[N_MEMORY]))
+		if (!nodes_subset(nodes, node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]))
 			goto out;
 	} else
 		nodes_clear(nodes);
@@ -3506,7 +3506,7 @@ int mpol_parse_str(char *str, struct mempolicy **mpol)
 		 * Default to online nodes with memory if no nodelist
 		 */
 		if (!nodelist)
-			nodes = node_states[N_MEMORY];
+			nodes = node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON];
 		break;
 	case MPOL_LOCAL:
 		/*
@@ -3901,6 +3901,9 @@ static int wi_node_notifier(struct notifier_block *nb,
 
 	switch (action) {
 	case NODE_ADDED_FIRST_MEMORY:
+		/* Weighted interleave spans only common memory. */
+		if (!node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON))
+			break;
 		err = sysfs_wi_node_add(nid);
 		if (err)
 			pr_err("failed to add sysfs for node%d during hotplug: %d\n",
@@ -3932,10 +3935,7 @@ static int __init add_weighted_interleave_group(struct kobject *mempolicy_kobj)
 	if (err)
 		goto err_put_kobj;
 
-	for_each_online_node(nid) {
-		if (!node_state(nid, N_MEMORY))
-			continue;
-
+	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {
 		err = sysfs_wi_node_add(nid);
 		if (err) {
 			pr_err("failed to add sysfs for node%d during init: %d\n",

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

N_MEMORY is overloaded with two meanings:
  1) a node has memory.
  2) a node's memory is reachable via ordinary allocation or
     an arbitrary MM service may use that memory.

Allow N_MEMORY to mean #1, and introduce N_MEMORY_COMMON to mean #2.

N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes contain "common memory" capable of being managed
arbitrarily by the kernel MM based solely on zone membership. Following
commits convert relevant N_MEMORY users to N_MEMORY_COMMON.

Expose the state via `has_common_memory` so userspace can identify
the memory available to ordinary allocations and common MM services.

Add has_memory to the docs while we're here.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node | 17 +++++++++++++++++
 Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst        |  8 +++++++-
 drivers/base/node.c                         |  2 ++
 include/linux/nodemask.h                    |  9 ++++++++-
 mm/page_alloc.c                             |  3 +++
 5 files changed, 37 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node b/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node
index 2d0e023f22a7..0a2cf3088233 100644
--- a/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node
+++ b/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node
@@ -10,6 +10,15 @@ Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
 Description:
 		Nodes that are online.
 
+What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_memory
+Date:		December 2012
+Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
+Description:
+		Nodes that have memory.
+
+		This memory may or may not be reachable via standard
+		allocations, see has_common_memory for details.
+
 What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_normal_memory
 Date:		October 2002
 Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
@@ -29,6 +38,14 @@ Description:
 		Nodes that have regular or high memory.
 		Depends on CONFIG_HIGHMEM.
 
+What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_common_memory
+Date:		November 2026
+Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
+Description:
+		Nodes whose memory ordinary allocations may use without
+		requesting the node explicitly, and that kernel memory
+		management services manage.
+
 What:		/sys/devices/system/node/nodeX
 Date:		October 2002
 Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
diff --git a/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst b/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
index 2e67e8b23a99..86a7d6080535 100644
--- a/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
+++ b/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
@@ -168,7 +168,12 @@ nodes with particular properties as defined by ``enum node_states``:
   The node has regular or high memory. When ``CONFIG_HIGHMEM`` is disabled
   aliased to ``N_NORMAL_MEMORY``.
 ``N_MEMORY``
-  The node has memory(regular, high, movable)
+  The node has online memory (regular, high, movable).  This is a topology and
+  accounting state. Presence in this mask does not mean ordinary allocations
+  can use the node's memory. See ``N_MEMORY_COMMON``.
+``N_MEMORY_COMMON``
+  Ordinary allocations and memory management services may use the node's
+  memory.
 ``N_CPU``
   The node has one or more CPUs
 ``N_GENERIC_INITIATOR``
@@ -184,6 +189,7 @@ For example, for node 2 with normal memory and CPUs, bit 2 will be set in ::
   node_states[N_NORMAL_MEMORY]
   node_states[N_HIGH_MEMORY]
   node_states[N_MEMORY]
+  node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]
   node_states[N_CPU]
 
 For various operations possible with nodemasks please refer to
diff --git a/drivers/base/node.c b/drivers/base/node.c
index dcdc8626627a..cc6696d1390f 100644
--- a/drivers/base/node.c
+++ b/drivers/base/node.c
@@ -965,6 +965,7 @@ static struct node_attr node_state_attr[] = {
 	[N_HIGH_MEMORY] = _NODE_ATTR(has_high_memory, N_HIGH_MEMORY),
 #endif
 	[N_MEMORY] = _NODE_ATTR(has_memory, N_MEMORY),
+	[N_MEMORY_COMMON] = _NODE_ATTR(has_common_memory, N_MEMORY_COMMON),
 	[N_CPU] = _NODE_ATTR(has_cpu, N_CPU),
 	[N_GENERIC_INITIATOR] = _NODE_ATTR(has_generic_initiator,
 					   N_GENERIC_INITIATOR),
@@ -978,6 +979,7 @@ static struct attribute *node_state_attrs[] = {
 	&node_state_attr[N_HIGH_MEMORY].attr.attr,
 #endif
 	&node_state_attr[N_MEMORY].attr.attr,
+	&node_state_attr[N_MEMORY_COMMON].attr.attr,
 	&node_state_attr[N_CPU].attr.attr,
 	&node_state_attr[N_GENERIC_INITIATOR].attr.attr,
 	NULL
diff --git a/include/linux/nodemask.h b/include/linux/nodemask.h
index 90bdcffa42ea..c3b984105bd1 100644
--- a/include/linux/nodemask.h
+++ b/include/linux/nodemask.h
@@ -398,7 +398,14 @@ enum node_states {
 #else
 	N_HIGH_MEMORY = N_NORMAL_MEMORY,
 #endif
-	N_MEMORY,		/* The node has memory(regular, high, movable) */
+	/*
+	 * N_MEMORY indicates online memory exists on the node - it is used
+	 * to manage per-node meta-data and topology decisions.
+	 * N_MEMORY_COMMON indicates whether the node can satisfy arbitrary
+	 * allocations and whether a service should manage that node's folios.
+	 */
+	N_MEMORY,		/* the node has memory */
+	N_MEMORY_COMMON,	/* common pool (fallback zonelist) */
 	N_CPU,		/* The node has one or more cpus */
 	N_GENERIC_INITIATOR,	/* The node has one or more Generic Initiators */
 	NR_NODE_STATES
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 88d507f93b1a..ddb04b72a160 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -203,6 +203,7 @@ nodemask_t node_states[NR_NODE_STATES] __read_mostly = {
 	[N_HIGH_MEMORY] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 #endif
 	[N_MEMORY] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
+	[N_MEMORY_COMMON] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 	[N_CPU] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 #endif	/* NUMA */
 };
@@ -211,10 +212,12 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL(node_states);
 void __meminit node_set_memory_state(int nid)
 {
 	node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY);
+	node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON);
 }
 
 void __meminit node_clear_memory_state(int nid)
 {
+	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON);
 	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY);
 }
 

--

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

do_migrate_range() / alloc_migration_target() is only capable of
allocating memory on N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes. The destination nodemask
presently starts with N_MEMORY and removes the source-node.

In the current code, if the destination mask becomes empty, the source
node is restored to allow migration during partial offlining.

Consider this configuration:
  Node0 = N_MEMORY_COMMON
  Node1 = N_MEMORY, not N_MEMORY_COMMON

Node 1 keeps the destination mask non-empty, despite being unreachable.
This leaves migration with no usable destination because the source
node is not an eligible allocation target.

Restrict the hot-unplug migration target-list to N_MEMORY_COMMON so it
reflects the nodes the allocator can reach.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/memory_hotplug.c | 8 ++++----
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/memory_hotplug.c b/mm/memory_hotplug.c
index e5cb770e4b09..1d3d1792074c 100644
--- a/mm/memory_hotplug.c
+++ b/mm/memory_hotplug.c
@@ -1926,7 +1926,7 @@ static void do_migrate_range(unsigned long start_pfn, unsigned long end_pfn)
 		folio_put(folio);
 	}
 	if (!list_empty(&source)) {
-		nodemask_t nmask = node_states[N_MEMORY];
+		nodemask_t nmask = node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON];
 		struct migration_target_control mtc = {
 			.nmask = &nmask,
 			.gfp_mask = GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_MOVABLE | __GFP_RETRY_MAYFAIL,
@@ -1941,9 +1941,9 @@ static void do_migrate_range(unsigned long start_pfn, unsigned long end_pfn)
 		mtc.nid = folio_nid(list_first_entry(&source, struct folio, lru));
 
 		/*
-		 * try to allocate from a different node but reuse this node
-		 * if there are no other online nodes to be used (e.g. we are
-		 * offlining a part of the only existing node)
+		 * try to allocate from a different common node but reuse this
+		 * node if there are no other common nodes to be used (e.g. we
+		 * are offlining a part of the only common node)
 		 */
 		node_clear(mtc.nid, nmask);
 		if (nodes_empty(nmask))

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Memory outside N_MEMORY_COMMON is outside the ordinary allocation pool
and cannot be a generic demotion source or destination.

Build demotion paths and the default DRAM performance reference from
N_MEMORY_COMMON rather than every node that has memory, and do not
assign other nodes to a memory tier through the generic hotplug path.

Removing a node's memory already resets its demotion targets, so a node
that unplugs and returns outside N_MEMORY_COMMON keeps none.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/memory-tiers.c | 23 ++++++++++++-----------
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+), 11 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/memory-tiers.c b/mm/memory-tiers.c
index 7fc56a8c6651..97d5ecefd89f 100644
--- a/mm/memory-tiers.c
+++ b/mm/memory-tiers.c
@@ -370,7 +370,8 @@ int next_demotion_node(int node, const nodemask_t *allowed_mask)
 	 * closest demotion target.
 	 */
 	nodes_complement(mask, *allowed_mask);
-	return find_next_best_node_in(node, &mask, &node_states[N_MEMORY]);
+	return find_next_best_node_in(node, &mask,
+				      &node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]);
 }
 
 static void disable_all_demotion_targets(void)
@@ -405,7 +406,7 @@ static void dump_demotion_targets(void)
 {
 	int node;
 
-	for_each_node_state(node, N_MEMORY) {
+	for_each_node_state(node, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {
 		struct memory_tier *memtier = __node_get_memory_tier(node);
 		nodemask_t preferred = node_demotion[node].preferred;
 
@@ -441,7 +442,7 @@ static void establish_demotion_targets(void)
 
 	disable_all_demotion_targets();
 
-	for_each_node_state(node, N_MEMORY) {
+	for_each_node_state(node, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {
 		best_distance = -1;
 		nd = &node_demotion[node];
 
@@ -459,7 +460,7 @@ static void establish_demotion_targets(void)
 		 * nodelist to skip list so that we find the best node from the
 		 * memtier nodelist.
 		 */
-		nodes_andnot(tier_nodes, node_states[N_MEMORY], tier_nodes);
+		nodes_andnot(tier_nodes, node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON], tier_nodes);
 
 		/*
 		 * Find all the nodes in the memory tier node list of same best distance.
@@ -468,7 +469,7 @@ static void establish_demotion_targets(void)
 		 */
 		do {
 			target = find_next_best_node_in(node, &tier_nodes,
-							&node_states[N_MEMORY]);
+							&node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]);
 			if (target == NUMA_NO_NODE)
 				break;
 
@@ -507,7 +508,7 @@ static void establish_demotion_targets(void)
 	 * allocation to a set of nodes that is closer the above selected
 	 * preferred node.
 	 */
-	lower_tier = node_states[N_MEMORY];
+	lower_tier = node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON];
 	list_for_each_entry(memtier, &memory_tiers, list) {
 		/*
 		 * Keep removing current tier from lower_tier nodes,
@@ -554,7 +555,7 @@ static struct memory_tier *set_node_memory_tier(int node)
 
 	lockdep_assert_held_once(&memory_tier_lock);
 
-	if (!node_state(node, N_MEMORY))
+	if (!node_state(node, N_MEMORY_COMMON))
 		return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);
 
 	mt_calc_adistance(node, &adist);
@@ -706,8 +707,8 @@ static int __init memory_tier_late_init(void)
 	get_online_mems();
 	guard(mutex)(&memory_tier_lock);
 
-	/* Assign each uninitialized N_MEMORY node to a memory tier. */
-	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY) {
+	/* Assign each uninitialized common memory node to a memory tier. */
+	for_each_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {
 		/*
 		 * Some device drivers may have initialized
 		 * memory tiers, potentially bringing memory nodes
@@ -929,8 +930,8 @@ static int __init memory_tier_init(void)
 	if (IS_ERR(default_dram_type))
 		panic("%s() failed to allocate default DRAM tier\n", __func__);
 
-	/* Record nodes with memory and CPU to set default DRAM performance. */
-	nodes_and(default_dram_nodes, node_states[N_MEMORY],
+	/* Record common-memory nodes with CPUs for default DRAM performance. */
+	nodes_and(default_dram_nodes, node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON],
 		  node_states[N_CPU]);
 
 	hotplug_node_notifier(memtier_hotplug_callback, MEMTIER_HOTPLUG_PRI);

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

move_pages(2) places user memory on a node the caller picks. As with
memory policies, the destination should be general purpose memory.

Reject a destination outside N_MEMORY_COMMON with -ENODEV, exactly
the same as a node without memory is rejected today.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/migrate.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/mm/migrate.c b/mm/migrate.c
index 65869b8acec5..208788b130fa 100644
--- a/mm/migrate.c
+++ b/mm/migrate.c
@@ -2411,7 +2411,7 @@ static int do_pages_move(struct mm_struct *mm, nodemask_t task_nodes,
 		err = -ENODEV;
 		if (node < 0 || node >= MAX_NUMNODES)
 			goto out_flush;
-		if (!node_state(node, N_MEMORY))
+		if (!node_state(node, N_MEMORY_COMMON))
 			goto out_flush;
 
 		err = -EACCES;

--

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

DAMOS migration actions move folios to a node the user picks. As with
move_pages(2), the destination should be general purpose memory.

Reject a destination outside N_MEMORY_COMMON, exactly the same as a
node without memory is rejected today.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/damon/ops-common.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/mm/damon/ops-common.c b/mm/damon/ops-common.c
index 2216a0023154..15cabc79613b 100644
--- a/mm/damon/ops-common.c
+++ b/mm/damon/ops-common.c
@@ -498,7 +498,7 @@ unsigned long damon_migrate_pages(struct list_head *folio_list, int target_nid)
 		return nr_migrated;
 
 	if (target_nid < 0 || target_nid >= MAX_NUMNODES ||
-			!node_state(target_nid, N_MEMORY)) {
+			!node_state(target_nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON)) {
 		damon_putback_folio_list(folio_list);
 		return nr_migrated;
 	}

--
